title: Designing Promotional Social Media Graphics
short_description: Create a set of three social media banners to promote an affiliate product.
business_problem: Static links are easily ignored; eye-catching visuals are required to capture attention on busy social feeds.

instruction.overview: Design three banners optimized for different platforms (e.g., Instagram, Facebook, and Pinterest) for one product.
steps: Select an affiliate product and its primary brand colors.
Create a Square banner for Instagram (1080x1080).
Create a Vertical banner for Pinterest or Stories (1080x1920).
Include a clear 'Shop Now' or 'Learn More' button design on each graphic.
Ensure the product name and its biggest benefit are clearly visible.
deliverables: A single PDF or image file showing all three designs.
submission_requirements: Submit a single PNG or PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the legibility of the text and the strength of the visual call-to-action.

title: Drafting an Ethical Disclosure Policy
short_description: Write a clear affiliate disclosure statement to comply with legal and ethical standards.
business_problem: Failure to disclose affiliate relationships can lead to legal penalties and loss of audience trust.

instruction.overview: You will draft a custom affiliate disclosure for a blog or social media profile that explains your relationship with brands.
steps: Research standard FTC guidelines for affiliate disclosures.
Draft a 'Short' version (for social media bios/captions).
Draft a 'Long' version (for a dedicated blog page).
Ensure the tone is honest and reassuring for the reader.
Include an explanation that affiliate links do not increase the price for the buyer.
deliverables: A document containing both the short and long disclosure versions.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The language should be clear, non-jargon, and prominently state the nature of the partnership.

title: Link Organization and UTM Tracking Log
short_description: Create a structured spreadsheet to manage affiliate links and track their performance source.
business_problem: Without organized tracking, it is impossible to know which platform (e.g., YouTube vs Blog) is generating sales.

instruction.overview: Build a master link log for 10 products with source-specific tracking variables.
steps: Create columns for Product Name, Original Link, and Target Platform.
Define a naming convention for tracking IDs (e.g., [Project]-[Source]-2026).
Generate 10 unique tracking links using UTM parameters.
Include a column for 'Cloaked Link' suggestions (e.g., [yoursite.com/go/product](https://yoursite.com/go/product)).
Enter 5 rows of dummy data showing hypothetical clicks and sales per link.
deliverables: A structured Excel spreadsheet with 10 managed links.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for consistency in the tracking ID naming convention.

title: Product Comparison and Ranking Table
short_description: Create a detailed comparison chart for three competing products to help buyers choose.
business_problem: Buyers are often overwhelmed by choice; a comparative analysis helps them make quick decisions, leading to higher conversions.

instruction.overview: Analyze three competing products in a single category and present them in a 'Best Overall', 'Best Budget', and 'Premium' format.
steps: Choose a product category (e.g., Wireless Earbuds).
Identify at least 5 key features to compare (e.g., Price, Battery Life, Warranty).
Fill in the data for three specific models.
Assign a 'Value Score' from 1-10 for each product.
Label one product as the 'Overall Winner' and another as 'Best Value'.
deliverables: A comparative analysis spreadsheet or formatted PDF table.
submission_requirements: Submit as an Excel file or PDF.
starter_resources: How to create product comparison tables
instruction.evaluation_notes: The criteria for the 'Winner' must be clearly justified by the data in the table.

title: Lead Magnet and Affiliate Welcome Sequence
short_description: Design a 3-email sequence that provides value before pitching an affiliate product.
business_problem: Directly pitching products to new subscribers often leads to high unsubscribes; nurturing the relationship first is essential.

instruction.overview: Write three emails: a welcome email with a free resource, a value-add tip email, and a final affiliate pitch email.
steps: Define a 'Lead Magnet' (e.g., a free PDF checklist) that relates to your niche.
Write Email 1: Delivering the resource and introducing yourself.
Write Email 2: Sharing a helpful tip that solves a problem without selling anything.
Write Email 3: Introducing the affiliate product as the ultimate solution to the problem.
Include catchy subject lines for all three emails.
deliverables: A document containing the 3-email sequence.
starter_resources: How to write effective welcome emails
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the transition from 'pure value' in email 2 to the 'pitch' in email 3.

title: Product Table Landing Page
short_description: Code a clean, responsive HTML/CSS landing page featuring a comparison table.
business_problem: Affiliate marketers need high-converting, mobile-friendly pages to showcase their top-recommended products.

instruction.overview: Build a single-page website that features a 'Top 3 Recommendations' table with clickable buttons.
steps: Create an HTML structure with a header, a comparison table, and a footer.
Use CSS Flexbox or Grid to make the table responsive on mobile devices.
Style the 'Affiliate Buttons' with hover effects to make them stand out.
Ensure all external links open in a new tab.
Include a simple footer with your Affiliate Disclosure statement.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing index.html and style.css.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for mobile responsiveness and clean code indentation.

title: Multi-Network Commission Tracking Dashboard
short_description: Develop a visual dashboard in Excel to track sales and ROI across multiple affiliate networks.
business_problem: Managing data from Amazon, ShareASale, and Impact in different places makes it hard to see the 'big picture' of profitability.

instruction.overview: Create a visual dashboard that aggregates performance data from three different networks.
steps: Set up a raw data tab to record Clicks, Sales, and Commission for 3 networks.
Use formulas to calculate Earnings Per Click (EPC) and Conversion Rate per network.
Create a 'Summary' tab with a Bar Chart comparing total revenue by network.
Add a Pie Chart showing the 'Distribution of Clicks' across your traffic sources.
Create an 'ROI Calculator' section where you input ad spend to find net profit.
deliverables: An Excel file with an interactive visual dashboard.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The charts must update automatically when new data is added to the raw data tab.

title: Simple Link Status Validator
short_description: Write a Python script that checks a list of affiliate URLs to ensure they are still active.
business_problem: Expired affiliate links or 404 errors lead to lost commissions and poor user experience.

instruction.overview: Develop a script that reads a list of URLs from a text file and reports which ones are broken.
steps: Create a text file with 5 sample URLs (include one intentionally 'dead' link).
Write a Python script using the 'requests' library to ping each URL.
Capture the HTTP status code (e.g., 200 for OK, 404 for Not Found).
Print a clean report showing 'Active' or 'Broken' for each link.
Add error handling to prevent the script from crashing if a site is down.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the .py script and sample text file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The script should clearly distinguish between successful responses and errors.

title: Professional Business Email Suite
short_description: Draft a set of professional emails for common workplace scenarios.
business_problem: Poorly phrased emails lead to misunderstandings, lost opportunities, and a lack of professional credibility.

instruction.overview: You will draft four specific emails: a project update, a meeting request, an apology for a delay, and an introduction.
steps: Select a professional tone suitable for a corporate environment.
Write a 150-word project status update for a manager.
Draft a concise meeting invitation for a cross-functional team.
Write a polite apology email regarding a missed deadline with a proposed solution.
Ensure every email has a clear, descriptive subject line and a professional sign-off.
deliverables: A document containing all four email drafts.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the balance between politeness and brevity.

title: Effective Meeting Minutes Documentation
short_description: Transcribe and summarize a meeting into a professional 'Action Items' document.
business_problem: Meetings often end without clear outcomes because the discussion wasn't properly documented.

instruction.overview: Use a provided 10-minute meeting transcript (or recording) to create a structured minutes document.
steps: List the date, time, and hypothetical attendees.
Summarize the main discussion points for each agenda item.
Create a clear table for 'Action Items' including the task, owner, and due date.
List any decisions made during the meeting.
Keep the language objective and neutral.
deliverables: A formal Meeting Minutes document.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The document must be scannable and focus on outcomes rather than a word-for-word transcript.

title: The Active Listening Self-Audit
short_description: Analyze a conversation to identify listening barriers and improvement areas.
business_problem: Most communication failures happen because people 'listen to respond' rather than 'listen to understand'.

instruction.overview: Record yourself in a 5-minute conversation and analyze your listening habits.
steps: Engage in a 5-minute conversation with a peer on a neutral topic.
Identify 3 instances where you used verbal or non-verbal cues to show you were listening.
Note any listening barriers you experienced (e.g., distraction, interrupting).
Write 3 'Paraphrasing' statements you could have used to clarify the other person's points.
Summarize your findings in a brief report.
deliverables: A 2-page self-audit report.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation is based on the depth of self-reflection.

title: Constructive Feedback Templates
short_description: Create a set of templates for giving and receiving performance feedback.
business_problem: Managers often avoid giving feedback because they don't know how to phrase it without sounding critical.

instruction.overview: Develop four feedback scripts based on the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model.
steps: Research the SBI (Situation, Behavior, Impact) model for feedback.
Write one script for positive feedback regarding a completed project.
Write one script for constructive feedback regarding a missed deadline.
Draft a template for 'Receiving Feedback' to show you are open to growth.
Include a 'Follow-up' plan for the constructive scenario.
deliverables: A document containing four feedback templates.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The feedback must be specific, objective, and actionable.

title: Workplace Conflict Resolution Analysis
short_description: Analyze a conflict case study and propose a step-by-step resolution strategy.
business_problem: Unresolved workplace conflicts decrease team morale and lead to high employee turnover.

instruction.overview: Read a provided case study about two colleagues with different work styles and propose a solution.
steps: Identify the root cause of the conflict in the case study.
List the perspectives and needs of both parties involved.
Outline a 5-step mediation process to bring the parties together.
Propose a 'Win-Win' outcome that addresses both parties' concerns.
Draft a 'Commitment Agreement' for both colleagues to sign.
deliverables: A 3-page conflict resolution proposal.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluate based on the fairness and feasibility of the proposed solution.

title: Non-Verbal Communication Video Report
short_description: Analyze a professional presentation video to identify the impact of body language.
business_problem: Up to 90% of communication is non-verbal; poor body language can undermine a speaker's message.

instruction.overview: Watch a 10-minute TED talk and write a report on the speaker's non-verbal communication.
steps: Identify 3 specific positive non-verbal cues used by the speaker.
Identify 2 non-verbal 'distractions' (e.g., excessive hand-waving, monotone voice).
Analyze how the speaker's body language changed during the 'climax' of their talk.
Comment on the speaker's use of pauses and silence for effect.
Provide 3 actionable tips for someone wanting to mimic the speaker's strengths.
deliverables: A 3-page visual analysis report.
starter_resources: The power of non-verbal communication guide
instruction.evaluation_notes: Look for specific timestamps to support the observations.

title: Internal Communications Newsletter Layout
short_description: Design and write the content for a monthly company-wide newsletter.
business_problem: Internal silos form when employees don't know what other departments are doing.

instruction.overview: Create a 2-page internal newsletter that includes an 'Employee Spotlight' and a 'CEO Update'.
steps: Select a professional layout using Canva, Word, or Figma.
Write a 300-word lead story about a major company milestone.
Draft a 150-word interview with a staff member ('Employee Spotlight').
Include a 'Calendar' section for upcoming team events.
Use consistent brand colors and fonts throughout the design.
deliverables: A 2-page visual newsletter.
submission_requirements: Submit a PDF or high-resolution PNG.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The newsletter should be engaging, visual, and easy to read.

title: Crisis Communication Response Kit
short_description: Develop a communication plan for a fictional service outage or PR issue.
business_problem: Delayed or defensive responses during a crisis can permanently damage a brand's reputation.

instruction.overview: Create a 5-page kit for a tech company experiencing a 4-hour data outage.
steps: Draft an immediate 'Holding Statement' for social media (Twitter/X).
Write a formal apology email to be sent to all paying customers.
Identify 3 key stakeholders and tailor a message for each (Employees, Investors, Customers).
Develop a 12-hour timeline of communication updates.
List 5 'Do's and Don'ts' for company representatives speaking to the press.
deliverables: A comprehensive Crisis Communication Kit (PDF).
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluate the speed, tone, and transparency of the proposed responses.

title: Cross-Cultural Remote Team Strategy
short_description: Develop a guide for effective communication within a globally distributed team.
business_problem: Cultural differences in communication styles can lead to unintended friction and low productivity.

instruction.overview: You will create a 'Team Manual' for a startup with employees in Pakistan, Germany, and the USA.
steps: Research the communication styles (High-context vs Low-context) of the three cultures.
Propose a 'Meeting Etiquette' guide that respects different time zones and cultural norms.
Define 3 rules for 'Asynchronous Communication' to avoid constant pings.
Outline a process for resolving cross-cultural misunderstandings.
Draft a 'Glossary of Common Terms' to ensure technical jargon is understood by all.
deliverables: A 4-page Cross-Cultural Communication Manual.
starter_resources: The Culture Map by Erin Meyer summary
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the inclusivity and practicality of the rules.

title: Executive Pitch: Selling a New System
short_description: Create a persuasive pitch deck and script to convince management to adopt a new tool.
business_problem: Good ideas often fail to launch because employees can't articulate the 'Value Proposition' to decision-makers.

instruction.overview: Develop a 10-slide pitch deck and a 5-minute script for introducing a new AI-support tool to the CEO.
steps: Identify the 'Pain Point' the new tool will solve.
Draft a 10-slide presentation (Problem, Solution, Cost, ROI, etc.).
Write a 500-word script to accompany the slides, focusing on persuasive hooks.
Include an 'FAQ and Objection Handling' section at the end of the script.
Ensure the visual design of the slides is professional and minimal.
deliverables: A 10-slide presentation PDF and a separate pitch script document.
submission_requirements: Submit both files in a single .zip upload.
starter_resources: How to pitch to an executive guide
The art of the value proposition
instruction.evaluation_notes: The pitch must focus on business outcomes (ROI) rather than just technical features.

title: Small Business Chart of Accounts Design
short_description: Organize the financial structure for a new retail store by setting up essential accounts.
business_problem: New businesses often have disorganized ledgers, making it impossible to track where money is actually going.

instruction.overview: You will design a complete Chart of Accounts for a fictional local gift shop.
steps: Select a retail business model and define its primary revenue source.
List 5 Asset accounts including Cash and Inventory.
List 3 Liability accounts including Accounts Payable.
Create 10 specific Expense accounts relevant to retail (e.g., Rent, Utilities).
Assign a logical numbering system to all accounts.
deliverables: A structured list of accounts with categories and numbers.
submission_requirements: Submit as a single .docx or .pdf file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct categorization of assets versus expenses.

title: Recording Daily Cash and Credit Sales
short_description: Simulate the daily entry of sales transactions and tax calculations.
business_problem: Failure to record daily sales accurately leads to discrepancies in cash flow and incorrect tax filings.

instruction.overview: Prepare a sales log for one day of business operations for a cafe.
steps: Create a table for 10 individual customer transactions.
Include columns for Item Name, Quantity, Price, and Sales Tax (8%).
Calculate the total for each transaction using formulas.
Categorize each sale by payment method (Cash vs. Credit Card).
Calculate the final daily total and total tax collected.
deliverables: A spreadsheet showing the daily sales transactions.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Mathematical accuracy in the formulas is the top priority.

title: Managing Vendor Invoices and Bills
short_description: Learn to enter and track money owed to suppliers to maintain good credit.
business_problem: Late payments to vendors can result in late fees and strained supplier relationships.

instruction.overview: You will draft a vendor management plan for three monthly bills.
steps: Identify 3 typical vendors for a service business (e.g., Internet, Rent, Office Supplies).
Record the bill date, amount, and payment terms (e.g., Net 30).
Assign each bill to the correct expense category.
Set a 'Remind Date' for each bill to ensure on-time payment.
Draft a short rule for how to handle disputed invoices.
deliverables: A document containing the vendor list and tracking rules.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Ensure due dates are calculated correctly based on the terms.

title: Manual Bank Reconciliation Simulation
short_description: Compare a bank statement to internal records to identify and fix errors.
business_problem: Bank balances often differ from internal books due to pending checks or bank fees.

instruction.overview: Perform a reconciliation between a provided bank statement and a company ledger.
steps: Review a list of 10 transactions from the company records.
Identify 3 items on the bank statement NOT in the records (e.g., monthly service fee).
Identify 2 checks that have been written but not yet 'cleared' by the bank.
Calculate the 'Adjusted Bank Balance' using the formula.
Write a 1-paragraph summary of why the two balances differed.
deliverables: A document showing the adjustment steps and the final reconciled balance.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The final adjusted book balance must equal the adjusted bank balance.

title: Inventory Valuation and Tracking Log
short_description: Track the flow of goods and calculate the value of remaining stock.
business_problem: Poor inventory tracking leads to 'stockouts' or overstocking, both of which hurt business profit.

instruction.overview: Create an inventory tracking sheet for 5 products using a weighted average cost method.
steps: Define 5 specific products with starting quantities and costs.
Record 2 purchase transactions from suppliers.
Record 3 sales transactions and update remaining quantities.
Calculate the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) for each sale.
Calculate the final 'Inventory Asset' value at the end of the period.
deliverables: An Excel file with formulas for quantity and valuation.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Formulas must correctly deduct quantities based on sales entries.

title: Comparative Profit and Loss Analysis
short_description: Compare two months of financial performance to identify trends and anomalies.
business_problem: Looking at one month in isolation doesn't tell a business owner if they are growing or failing.

instruction.overview: Analyze two provided Profit & Loss statements and write a performance report.
steps: Calculate the absolute dollar change between Month 1 and Month 2 for all main categories.
Calculate the percentage change for Total Revenue and Total Expenses.
Identify the top 3 expense categories that increased the most.
Write a 200-word summary explaining why the profit increased or decreased.
Suggest two cost-cutting measures based on the data.
deliverables: A 2-page PDF analysis report with tables and summary.
starter_resources: How to read a P&L statement
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluated based on the accuracy of the percentage change calculations.

title: Small Team Payroll Processing Map
short_description: Calculate gross pay, taxes, and net pay for a team of three employees.
business_problem: Incorrect payroll calculations can lead to legal penalties and unhappy employees.

instruction.overview: Map out the payroll cycle and calculations for a 3-person team for one month.
steps: Define hourly rates and hours worked for 3 employees (include one with overtime).
Calculate Gross Pay for each person.
Deduct a flat 15% for Federal Income Tax and 7.65% for FICA.
Calculate the total 'Employer Tax' liability for the company.
Draft a process flow showing when payments are made and when taxes are filed.
deliverables: A payroll calculation document and process flowchart.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Calculation accuracy and logical flow of the map are essential.

title: Executive Financial Reporting Dashboard
short_description: Design a visual dashboard that highlights critical business health metrics.
business_problem: Executives don't have time to read 50-page reports; they need a visual snapshot of performance.

instruction.overview: Design a mockup of a financial dashboard that tracks 4 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
steps: Identify 4 KPIs for a service-based business (e.g., Days Sales Outstanding, Cash Flow).
Design a visual layout (using Canva, Figma, or Word) showing these metrics.
Explain which QuickBooks reports would be used to pull each metric.
Define 'Target Ranges' (Red/Green zones) for each KPI.
Add a 150-word guide on how an executive should use this dashboard to make decisions.
deliverables: A single-page visual dashboard design and explanation PDF.
submission_requirements: Submit as a PNG or PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the relevance of the chosen KPIs to business health.

title: Quarterly Budget Variance Analysis
short_description: Create a 6-month budget and analyze deviations from actual results.
business_problem: Without a budget, businesses overspend in some areas and underinvest in others.

instruction.overview: Build a quarterly budget and analyze dummy 'actual' data to find variances.
steps: Create a 6-month budget spreadsheet with Revenue and 5 major Expense categories.
Enter 'Actual' data for the first 3 months with intentional variations.
Use formulas to calculate the 'Variance' (Budget minus Actual).
Label each variance as 'Favorable' or 'Unfavorable'.
Write a 300-word analysis on the cause of the largest variance and propose a budget adjustment.
deliverables: A multi-tab Excel file with budget comparisons and analysis.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluated based on the depth of the analysis explaining the 'unfavorable' outcomes.

title: Year-End Closing and Tax Audit Prep
short_description: Verify all account balances and prepare a checklist for a tax accountant.
business_problem: Poorly prepared books at year-end lead to higher accounting fees and a higher risk of IRS audits.

instruction.overview: Develop a professional year-end closing checklist and audit file for a small corporation.
steps: Create an 'Accounts Receivable Aging' summary to find past-due invoices.
Draft a list of 5 'Adjusting Journal Entries' for items like depreciation or prepaid rent.
Perform a final 'Trial Balance' check to ensure all debits and credits match.
Compile a checklist of required documents (e.g., bank statements, loan agreements).
Write a 1-page memo to the Tax Accountant summarizing the year's main financial events.
deliverables: A 5-page year-end closing and audit preparation PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Audit files must be organized logically for a third-party reviewer.

title: Competitor Analysis and Market Matrix
short_description: Identify and compare direct and indirect competitors for a new startup idea.
business_problem: New entrepreneurs often enter markets without knowing who their competitors are or how to differentiate their service.

instruction.overview: You will research 5 competitors for a chosen startup niche and map their strengths and weaknesses in a matrix.
steps: Pick a simple startup idea (e.g., a local delivery app or a niche subscription box).
Find 3 direct competitors and 2 indirect competitors.
List their primary features, pricing, and target audience.
Identify one 'Market Gap' where these competitors are failing to meet user needs.
Summarize your findings in a comparison table.
deliverables: A spreadsheet containing the competitor matrix and market gap summary.
starter_resources: Guide to direct vs indirect competitors
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the accuracy of the competitor categorization.

title: Business Model Canvas Draft
short_description: Map out the nine building blocks of a startup using the Business Model Canvas.
business_problem: Startup founders often have vague ideas that lack a clear plan for revenue or customer acquisition.

instruction.overview: Create a one-page business model overview for a fictional startup idea.
steps: Choose a simple product or service idea.
Identify the primary Value Proposition (what problem are you solving?).
Define the Customer Segments you are targeting.
Outline how the business will make money (Revenue Streams).
List the top 3 Key Partners needed to launch.
deliverables: A one-page document or image of the completed Business Model Canvas.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The Value Proposition must clearly match the identified Customer Segments.

title: Value Proposition and Elevator Pitch
short_description: Write a compelling value proposition and a 30-second elevator pitch for a startup.
business_problem: Founders struggle to explain their business quickly, leading to lost interest from potential partners or investors.

instruction.overview: You will draft a clear Value Proposition Statement and a short script for a verbal pitch.
steps: Describe the specific problem your startup solves in one sentence.
Write a 'Value Proposition' statement using the format: 'We help [X] to [Y] by doing [Z]'.
Draft a 100-word elevator pitch that includes a 'Hook' at the start.
Include a 'Call to Action' (what you want the listener to do next).
deliverables: A document containing the value proposition and the pitch script.
starter_resources: How to write an elevator pitch
instruction.evaluation_notes: The pitch should be conversational and easy to understand for a non-expert.

title: MVP Feature Prioritization Matrix
short_description: Decide which features are essential for a Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
business_problem: Startups often fail by spending too much time building complex features before testing if users want the product.

instruction.overview: List potential features for a new app and categorize them to define a 'Day 1' product.
steps: List 10 potential features for a chosen startup idea.
Score each feature (1-5) on 'User Value' and 'Development Effort'.
Identify the 'Must-Have' features for the MVP (Minimum Viable Product).
List the 'Nice-to-Have' features for future updates.
Explain in 2 sentences why the chosen MVP features are enough to launch.
deliverables: A spreadsheet containing the feature list and prioritization scores.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The MVP should include only the bare minimum required to solve the core problem.

title: Customer Persona and Interview Guide
short_description: Define the ideal customer and create a set of questions to validate your startup idea.
business_problem: Building for 'everyone' results in building for no one. Startups need deep insights into specific user pain points.

instruction.overview: You will create a detailed profile of a target customer and a script to interview them.
steps: Create a 'Customer Persona' including age, job, goals, and 3 specific frustrations.
Identify where this persona currently spends their time and money.
Write 10 open-ended interview questions that focus on the problem, not your solution.
Explain how you would find 5 people matching this persona to talk to.
Include a 'Red Flag' list of things that would prove your idea is wrong.
deliverables: A document containing the persona and the interview guide.
starter_resources: How to create a customer persona
instruction.evaluation_notes: Questions must be open-ended (avoid 'Would you use this?').

title: Pricing Strategy Comparison
short_description: Analyze different pricing models to find the best fit for a startup's revenue.
business_problem: Picking the wrong pricing model (e.g., subscription vs one-time) can kill a startup's cash flow or growth.

instruction.overview: Research three different pricing strategies and recommend one for a specific startup.
steps: Select a startup service (e.g., a photo editing app).
Compare 'Freemium', 'Flat Monthly Subscription', and 'Pay-per-use' models.
List 2 pros and 2 cons for each model based on the target audience.
Propose a 'Tiered' pricing structure (e.g., Basic, Pro, Enterprise).
Calculate the 'Break-even' point (how many users you need to cover costs).
deliverables: A pricing strategy report with the tiered structure proposal.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The recommendation must align with the target customer's ability to pay.

title: Go-to-Market (GTM) Launch Plan
short_description: Create a step-by-step roadmap for acquiring the first 100 customers.
business_problem: Startups often 'build and hope', but without a clear acquisition strategy, the product never gets used.

instruction.overview: Design a 30-day plan to find and convert your first 100 users/customers.
steps: Identify 3 primary channels for acquisition (e.g., LinkedIn outreach, Product Hunt, local events).
Define the 'Early Adopter' profile (who needs it MOST right now?).
Create a weekly timeline of tasks for the first month.
Draft one outreach message or ad copy for your top channel.
Set a 'Success Metric' for each of the 4 weeks.
deliverables: A 3-page GTM roadmap in PDF format.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The plan should be practical and low-budget.

title: Lean Startup Experiment Design
short_description: Design a 'Smoke Test' or landing page experiment to validate demand for a feature.
business_problem: Building a full feature based on a guess is expensive. Lean experiments prove demand with minimal effort.

instruction.overview: You will design a scientific experiment to test if people are willing to pay for a specific feature.
steps: State a 'Falsifiable Hypothesis' (e.g., 'At least 10% of visitors will click the Buy button').
Design the experiment layout (e.g., a simple landing page with a waitlist sign-up).
Define the 'Success Metric' and the 'Failure Metric'.
Identify the 'Cost of Experiment' in time and money (keep it very low).
Describe the 'Next Step' if the experiment succeeds versus if it fails.
deliverables: A detailed experiment design report (PDF).
submission_requirements: Submit as a single PDF file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The hypothesis must be measurable and clearly defined.

title: Basic Financial Projections for Startups
short_description: Create a 12-month revenue and expense forecast for a new business.
business_problem: Founders need to know when they will run out of money ('Burn Rate') to plan for funding or growth.

instruction.overview: Build a spreadsheet that shows how much money a startup will spend and earn in its first year.
steps: List monthly 'Fixed Costs' (rent, base software) and 'Variable Costs' (ads, cloud fees).
Estimate 'Customer Growth' based on a specific marketing spend.
Calculate monthly 'Gross Profit' and 'Net Profit'.
Determine the 'Runway' (how many months of operation) given a $5,000 starting budget.
Add a summary chart showing the profit/loss trend over 12 months.
deliverables: A 12-month financial projection spreadsheet.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Formulas must be linked correctly so that changing growth rates updates the whole sheet.

title: Startup Pitch Deck for Seed Funding
short_description: Design a 10-slide presentation that covers the essential story of a startup.
business_problem: Investors only spend a few minutes looking at a deck; it must be visually clean and tell a logical story.

instruction.overview: You will create a professional 10-slide deck based on the 'Sequoia Capital' pitch deck structure.
steps: Draft the content for 10 slides: Problem, Solution, Why Now, Market Size, Competition, Product, Business Model, Team, Financials, and 'The Ask'.
Use a consistent visual style (colors/fonts) across all slides.
Ensure each slide has one clear headline and minimal text.
Include a 'Market Size' (TAM/SAM/SOM) slide with realistic numbers.

title: Spotting Phishing and Email Scams
