business_problem: Financial software requires secure, encapsulated logic to manage account balances and transactions.

instruction.overview: Design an 'Account' class that maintains a balance and allows withdrawals and deposits via a console menu.
steps: Create an 'Account' class with a private balance field.
Implement a constructor to set an initial balance.
Add methods for 'deposit' and 'withdraw' with validation logic.
Write a main class to present a loop-based menu (Check Balance, Deposit, Withdraw, Exit).
Prevent users from withdrawing more than the available balance.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code files and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation focuses on proper use of access modifiers (private/public).

title: Library Book Search Engine
short_description: Develop a program to search for books in a list using titles or authors.
business_problem: Inventory management systems need efficient ways to filter and find specific items in large collections.

instruction.overview: Build a system that stores 'Book' objects in a list and allows a user to query them.
steps: Create a 'Book' class with Title and Author attributes.
Initialize an ArrayList and add 5-10 book objects.
Prompt the user to enter a search term.
Loop through the list and display books where the title or author matches the search term (case-insensitive).
Print a message if no books are found.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Ensure searching logic covers both title and author fields.

title: Text File Word Counter
short_description: Create a tool that reads a .txt file and counts the total number of words.
business_problem: Processing external data files is a core requirement for log analysis and content management systems.

instruction.overview: Develop a script that parses a local text file and outputs the word count to the console.
steps: Set up file reading using BufferedReader or Scanner.
Implement try-catch blocks to handle FileNotFound and IO exceptions.
Read the file line by line.
Split each line by whitespace to isolate words.
Maintain a running counter and display the final total.
deliverables: A .zip containing source code and a sample .txt file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The program should not crash if the file does not exist.

title: Employee Payroll Persistence System
short_description: Design an employee manager that saves payroll data to a CSV file.
business_problem: Enterprise applications must persist data across sessions to be useful for business operations.

instruction.overview: Build a system to add employees and their salaries, then export the entire list to a formatted CSV file.
steps: Create an 'Employee' base class and a 'Manager' subclass with inheritance.
Implement a list to store multiple employee objects.
Write a method that iterates through the list and formats data as 'Name, Salary'.
Use PrintWriter or BufferedWriter to save this data to 'payroll.csv'.
Include a README explaining how to open the resulting CSV in Excel.
deliverables: A .zip with all Java classes and a sample output CSV.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Writing to CSV files in Java
instruction.evaluation_notes: Correct implementation of class inheritance and file writing is key.

title: Product Inventory with Serialization
short_description: Implement a product tracker that saves the entire object state to a binary file.
business_problem: Saving complex object states (Serialization) allows apps to resume precisely where they left off.

instruction.overview: Create a 'Product' tracker that can save its current list of items to a file and load them back on startup.
steps: Ensure the 'Product' class implements the Serializable interface.
Write logic to 'Serialize' the ArrayList of products to an 'inventory.ser' file.
Write logic to 'Deserialize' (load) the file when the program starts.
Add functionality to add/remove products from the live list.
Provide a README explaining the benefit of binary serialization over plain text.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The program must handle cases where the data file is missing on the first run.

title: Basic Threaded Search Performance Test
short_description: Compare searching performance between a single thread and two threads.
business_problem: Modern applications utilize multi-core processors to increase speed; understanding threading is vital for performance tuning.

instruction.overview: Write a Java program that searches for a number in a large array using one thread vs. two parallel threads.
steps: Generate a large array (e.g., 10 million items) filled with random numbers.
Search for a target value using a standard single-threaded loop and measure the time.
Implement a searchable Runnable that processes half of the array.
Spawn two threads to search each half simultaneously and measure the combined time.
Output the performance difference to the console.
deliverables: A .zip with the multithreaded source code and a README analysis.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct use of thread.start() and thread.join().

title: Interactive Console Budget Tool
short_description: Create a command-line application to calculate monthly savings based on income and expenses.
business_problem: Individuals often fail to track their finances because they lack simple, lightweight tools to quickly calculate their remaining balance.

instruction.overview: Develop a C# console app that takes monthly income and a list of three expense categories to output a financial summary.
steps: Prompt the user to enter their total monthly income using Console.ReadLine().
Ask for expenses in three categories: Rent, Food, and Utilities.
Calculate the total expenses and the remaining monthly savings.
Check if the savings are negative and display a 'Warning' message if so.
Display the final balance formatted as currency.
deliverables: C# source file (.cs) containing the Program class.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Formatting strings as currency in C#
instruction.evaluation_notes: The program must handle non-numeric inputs without crashing (using TryParse is recommended).

title: Student Attendance Tracker
short_description: Build a script to store student names and check if they are present or absent.
business_problem: Manual attendance taking is prone to error and difficult to digitize for further analysis.

instruction.overview: Create a program that allows a teacher to enter names for a class and then mark each student as present or absent.
steps: Initialize an array to hold 5 student names.
Use a loop to populate the array with names from user input.
Iterate through the array and ask the teacher for each student: 'Present? (Y/N)'.
Count the total number of students marked 'Y'.
Display a final summary: 'Total Students: 5, Present: X, Absent: Y'.
deliverables: C# source file (.cs).
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Program should be case-insensitive for 'Y' and 'N' inputs.

title: Unit Conversion Multi-Tool
short_description: Create a console menu to convert distances and weights.
business_problem: Small businesses dealing with international shipping often need quick, internal tools for unit conversion.

instruction.overview: Build a menu-driven C# application that converts Kilometers to Miles and Grams to Ounces.
steps: Create a Main method with a switch-case to display conversion options.
Implement a method for Kilometer to Mile conversion (1 km = 0.621 miles).
Implement a method for Gram to Ounce conversion (1 g = 0.035 oz).
Use a while loop to allow the user to perform multiple conversions without restarting.
Ensure results are displayed to two decimal places.
deliverables: C# source file (.cs).
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Logic should handle invalid menu choices by showing an error message.

title: Random Password Generator CLI
short_description: Write a program that generates a secure random password of a user-defined length.
business_problem: Weak passwords are a major security risk; automation ensures complex passwords are used every time.

instruction.overview: Develop a tool that picks random characters from a string of allowed symbols to build a password.
steps: Define a string containing all allowed characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, symbols).
Prompt the user for the desired password length.
Use the Random class within a loop to select characters by index.
Concatenate the characters into a final string.
Display the generated password to the console.
deliverables: C# source file (.cs) and a README explaining the logic.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check that the password truly matches the user's requested length.

title: Employee Management OOP System
short_description: Implement an employee system using classes and inheritance for different staff types.
business_problem: Managing different employee roles (Salaried vs Hourly) requires a flexible code structure that avoids duplication.

instruction.overview: Design a base Employee class and two derived classes: HourlyEmployee and SalariedEmployee.
steps: Create a base 'Employee' class with common properties (Name, ID).
Add a virtual method 'CalculatePay()' in the base class.
Inherit 'HourlyEmployee' and override CalculatePay() using (Hours * Rate).
Inherit 'SalariedEmployee' and override CalculatePay() to return a fixed monthly amount.
Instantiate one of each in Main and print their names and calculated pay.
deliverables: A .zip containing the class files and a Program.cs.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct use of 'override' and 'base' keywords.

title: Digital Notes File Tracker
short_description: Develop a utility to write user notes to a local text file and read them back.
business_problem: Software systems often need to log data or save local settings between sessions without a full database.

instruction.overview: Create a simple note-taking CLI that saves data to a file named 'notes.txt'.
steps: Implement a menu: 1. Write Note, 2. View All Notes, 3. Exit.
Option 1 should take a string and append it to 'notes.txt' using File.AppendAllLines.
Option 2 should check if the file exists using File.Exists().
If it exists, read and display the entire file content; otherwise, show a 'No notes found' error.
Wrap file operations in try-catch blocks to handle potential IO errors.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The program should not crash if 'notes.txt' is open in another program.

title: Product Inventory with LINQ
short_description: Use LINQ to query and filter a list of products in a store inventory.
business_problem: Finding specific data within large collections is slow without structured querying like LINQ.

instruction.overview: Build a console app that manages a list of 'Product' objects and performs advanced filters using LINQ.
steps: Create a 'Product' class with Name, Category, and Price.
Populate a List<Product> with 10 sample items across different categories.
Use LINQ to find and display all products with a price greater than 100.
Use LINQ to list all products in a specific category (e.g., 'Electronics').
Sort the final display by price in descending order.
deliverables: A .zip file with the C# code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Queries must be efficient and use standard LINQ method or query syntax.

title: Persistent Task Manager with JSON
short_description: Build a task app that saves data to a JSON file using serialization.
business_problem: Modern applications require structured data persistence (JSON) to easily share data across different platforms.

instruction.overview: Create a tool to save a list of Task objects to a local JSON file and load them back on startup.
steps: Use the System.Text.Json namespace for serialization.
Create a 'TodoItem' class with Title and IsCompleted properties.
Write a method to serialize the List<TodoItem> into a string and save it to 'tasks.json'.
Write a method to read the file and deserialize it back into the list when the program starts.
Implement a simple menu to add/remove tasks before saving.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code and a sample JSON output.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The JSON file should be properly formatted (indented) for readability.

title: Parallel Prime Number Finder
short_description: Use multi-threading to find prime numbers in a large range and compare performance.
business_problem: CPU-intensive tasks can block the main application thread; parallel processing utilizes multi-core hardware to speed up calculations.

instruction.overview: Implement a prime number check across a large range (e.g., 1 to 100,000) using sequential and parallel methods.
steps: Write a sequential function that loops through numbers and finds primes, measuring time with a Stopwatch.
Rewrite the logic using Parallel.For or a List of Tasks to split the work.
Ensure results are stored in a thread-safe way (e.g., using lock or ConcurrentBag).
Display the time taken for both methods to the console.
Verify that both methods find the exact same number of primes.
deliverables: A .zip containing the multithreaded source code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Performance speedup in the parallel version should be noticeable on multi-core systems.

title: Contact Database with SQLite and Dapper
short_description: Create a lightweight local database application to store and search contact info.
business_problem: Enterprise-level apps require structured storage that can handle complex relationships and rapid searches.

instruction.overview: Build a console app that connects to a local SQLite database to perform CRUD operations on a Contacts table.
steps: Install the Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and Dapper NuGet packages.
Write code to create a 'Contacts' table (Name, Phone, Email) if it doesn't exist.
Implement an 'Add Contact' feature using a SQL INSERT statement via Dapper.
Implement a 'Search Contact' feature using a SQL SELECT query with parameters.
Include a 'Delete Contact' option to remove records by ID.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code and project file (.csproj).
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Proper use of parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection is mandatory.

title: Basic Web Page with Partial Includes
short_description: Create a simple multi-page website using PHP 'include' for the header and footer.
business_problem: Maintaining the same header and footer across many HTML files is difficult; PHP partials allow for centralized updates.

instruction.overview: You will develop a 3-page site (Home, About, Contact) that shares a single header.php and footer.php file.
steps: Create a header.php file containing the navigation menu.
Create a footer.php file with copyright info and links.
Build index.php, about.php, and contact.php files.
Use the PHP include() or require() function to pull the header and footer into each page.
Ensure navigation links work correctly between the pages.
deliverables: A functioning 3-page website structure.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the successful modularization of the layout elements.

title: Simple Contact Form Processor
short_description: Build a script to capture, validate, and display user data from an HTML form.
business_problem: Websites need to process user input safely while providing feedback to the sender.

instruction.overview: Create an HTML form and a PHP script that receives the data and prints a summary to the screen.
steps: Design a form with Name, Email, and Message fields.
Set the form action to point to a PHP processing script.
Use $_POST to capture the input data.
Implement basic validation to check if fields are empty.
Sanitize the output using htmlspecialchars() before displaying it back to the user.
deliverables: An HTML form and a PHP processing script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check that the validation correctly catches empty inputs.

title: Interactive BMI Calculator
short_description: Develop a PHP script that calculates Body Mass Index based on user weight and height.
business_problem: Interactive tools provide value to users and demonstrate logic processing on the server side.

instruction.overview: Create a tool that takes weight and height inputs and provides the BMI score and category.
steps: Build a form for numeric inputs (Weight in kg, Height in meters).
Perform the calculation in PHP: BMI = Weight / (Height * Height).
Round the result to one decimal place.
Use if-else statements to categorize the result (Underweight, Normal, Overweight).
Display the final score and category on the page.
deliverables: A functioning PHP calculator script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Ensure the script doesn't crash if height is entered as 0 (division by zero check).

title: Array-Based Dynamic Product List
short_description: Use PHP arrays to dynamically generate a product catalog table.
business_problem: Hard-coding HTML tables is inefficient; dynamic generation from data structures is the industry standard.

instruction.overview: Define an array of products and use a loop to render them into a clean HTML table.
steps: Create an associative array with 5 products (Name, Price, Category).
Write an HTML <table> structure.
Use a foreach loop in PHP to iterate through the array.
Output an HTML <tr> for every product in the array.
Apply basic CSS to make the table readable.
deliverables: A PHP file that renders an HTML table from an internal array.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for correct syntax when embedding PHP tags within HTML tags.

title: MySQL Database Information Fetcher
short_description: Connect to a MySQL database and fetch records to display on a webpage.
business_problem: Dynamic applications require the ability to retrieve and display information stored in relational databases.

instruction.overview: Use the PHP Data Objects (PDO) extension to connect to a local database and display a list of users or items.
steps: Set up a local MySQL database with a simple table (e.g., 'tasks').
Establish a connection using PDO with correct DSN, username, and password.
Write a SQL SELECT query to retrieve all records.
Execute the query and fetch the results into an array.
Loop through the results to display them in a list on the webpage.
deliverables: A .zip containing the PHP script and a .sql export of your table structure.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the use of modern PDO methods over legacy 'mysql_' functions.

title: Secure User Registration with PHP/MySQL
short_description: Create a sign-up form that securely hashes passwords and saves them to a database.
business_problem: Storing plain-text passwords is a massive security risk; backend developers must know how to handle sensitive data correctly.

instruction.overview: Implement a registration flow that uses prepared statements to prevent SQL injection and secure hashing for passwords.
steps: Design a registration form (Username, Email, Password).
Capture the data and hash the password using password_hash().
Set up a PDO prepared statement with bindParam() or bindValue().
Execute the INSERT query to save the user.
Provide a success message or handle errors (like duplicate emails).
deliverables: Registration PHP file and a .sql schema file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Preventing SQL Injection with Prepared Statements
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation is based on the security of the implementation (no direct variable interpolation in SQL).

title: Simple Article Manager (CRUD)
short_description: Develop a system to create and view blog articles stored in a database.
business_problem: CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations are the core of most management systems and e-commerce backends.

instruction.overview: Build a two-page system: one to add a new article and one to list all existing articles.
steps: Create a 'posts' table in MySQL (id, title, content, created_at).
Build create_post.php with a form that saves data to the DB.
Build index.php that lists all posts with their title and date.
Include a 'Read More' link that takes users to a dynamic view_post.php page.
Use a URL parameter (e.g., ?id=1) to fetch the specific post.
deliverables: A .zip containing the code files and database export.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Building a simple CMS in PHP
instruction.evaluation_notes: The view_post.php script must use prepared statements to handle the ID parameter safely.

title: Image Gallery Upload Utility
short_description: Create a script that allows users to upload images and displays them in a grid.
business_problem: Handling file uploads is a complex advanced task that requires strict validation and directory management.

instruction.overview: Build a tool to upload photos to a 'uploads' folder and show them on the homepage.
steps: Create an HTML form with the correct enctype for file uploads.
Implement PHP logic to check file size and allowed extensions (e.g., .jpg, .png).
Generate a unique filename using uniqid() to prevent overwriting files.
Use move_uploaded_file() to save the image securely.
Write a loop to scan the 'uploads' folder and render every image inside an tag.
deliverables: PHP upload script, index display page, and 'uploads' directory.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: PHP glob() function for directory scanning
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for security measures against uploading malicious .php files disguised as images.

title: RESTful API for Product Catalog
short_description: Write a PHP script that outputs JSON data for a frontend application to consume.
business_problem: Modern web development often decouples the backend from the frontend; APIs are the bridge that connects them.

instruction.overview: Create an API endpoint that returns product data from a MySQL database in a structured JSON format.
steps: Set the PHP header to output 'application/json'.
Connect to the database and fetch all products.
Implement a simple filter where the user can provide a category via GET.
Use json_encode() to transform the results array into a string.
Include appropriate HTTP status codes (200 for success, 404 for not found).
deliverables: A PHP API script and a README explaining the URL parameters.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Creating a REST API with PHP
instruction.evaluation_notes: The output must be valid JSON that can be parsed by any external tool.

title: Session-Based Protected Dashboard
short_description: Implement a login-guarded dashboard using PHP sessions for state management.
business_problem: Apps need a way to remember users as they navigate between different pages (authentication persistence).

instruction.overview: Create a login page and a dashboard that is only accessible if the user is logged in.
steps: Implement a simple login form with fixed or DB-checked credentials.
If successful, start a session and store the username in $_SESSION.
Create dashboard.php that checks for the session variable at the top of the file.
If the session variable is missing, redirect the user back to the login page immediately.
Add a logout.php file that destroys the session and clears variables.
deliverables: A .zip containing the full authentication system.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct use of session_start() and the security of the redirection logic.

title: Interactive Welcome Greeting App
short_description: Create a React component that updates a greeting based on user input.
business_problem: Modern web interfaces need to feel personalized; learning how to sync input fields with displayed text is the core of React's state system.

instruction.overview: Build a small React application that asks for a user's name and displays a personalized greeting in real-time.
steps: Initialize a new React project using Vite or Create React App.
Create a text input field and a heading (H1) in the App component.
Implement the 'useState' hook to manage the user's name.
Write an event handler to update the state as the user types.
Display the state value within the heading (e.g., 'Hello, Salman!').
deliverables: A .zip file containing the project source code and configuration files.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct implementation of the controlled input pattern.

title: Digital Tally Counter
short_description: Develop a React app with increment, decrement, and reset functionality.
business_problem: Simple utility tools require precise state updates; this project demonstrates how to handle multiple event triggers safely.

instruction.overview: Create a visual counter where users can increase or decrease a number, ensuring it never goes below zero.
steps: Set up a React component with a state variable initialized to 0.
Add three buttons: '+', '-', and 'Reset'.
Implement logic to increment the number on '+' click.
Implement logic to decrement the number but prevent negative values.
Style the number to change color (e.g., green if positive, red if zero).
deliverables: A .zip file with the functional counter project.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Verify that the 'zero-floor' logic works correctly.

title: Team Profile Card Components
short_description: Build a reusable profile card component and render a list of team members.
business_problem: Websites need consistent UI for staff directories; reusable components reduce code duplication and errors.

instruction.overview: Design a 'ProfileCard' component that accepts name, role, and image URL as props and renders them in a grid.
steps: Define a 'ProfileCard' component in a separate file.
Create an array of 4 objects representing different team members.
In the main App component, use the .map() method to render a card for each member.
Pass the data from the array to the component via props.
Apply CSS to display the cards in a responsive layout.
deliverables: A .zip file containing the component and layout code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for the presence of unique 'key' props in the list mapping.

title: Searchable Item List
short_description: Build a component that filters an array of strings as the user types.
business_problem: Users need quick ways to find information in long lists; real-time filtering is a standard UX expectation.

instruction.overview: Develop an app that displays a list of 10 fruits or items and a search bar to filter the results.
steps: Create a state to track the search query string.
Define a static array of at least 10 items.
Write logic to filter the array based on whether the item includes the search query.
Ensure the search is case-insensitive.
Display only the matching items in a list below the search bar.
deliverables: A .zip file with the filtering app code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The list should update immediately upon typing without needing a submit button.

title: Dynamic Task Manager (To-Do List)
short_description: Create a fully functional task list with add and delete capabilities.
business_problem: Task management is a core application pattern; managing arrays in state is a fundamental intermediate skill.

instruction.overview: Build an app where users can type a task, add it to a list, and delete individual tasks when finished.
steps: Implement a state to hold an array of task objects (each with an id and text).
Create a function to add a new task using the spread operator to preserve existing state.
Create a function to delete a task by filtering the array for a specific id.
Include a 'Clear All' button to empty the array.
Add basic styling to differentiate between an empty state and an active list.
deliverables: A .zip file containing the complete source code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Verify that deleting one task does not accidentally delete others.

title: User Feedback Form with Validation
short_description: Build a feedback form that validates inputs before 'submitting' data.
business_problem: Forms are the primary way to collect customer data; invalid data causes backend errors and needs client-side prevention.

instruction.overview: Create a form for Name, Email, and Message that displays errors if requirements (like email format) aren't met.
steps: Set up an object-based state to manage all form fields simultaneously.
Implement a validation function that checks for empty fields and proper email structure.
Disable the 'Submit' button if validation fails or show red error text.
On successful submit, clear the form and log the data to the console.
Prevent the default browser form submission behavior.
deliverables: A .zip file with the source code and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The UI should provide immediate feedback if a field is invalid.

title: Themed Portfolio with Dark Mode
short_description: Implement a theme switcher that saves user preference to the browser.
business_problem: User experience is enhanced by supporting system-level preferences like dark mode.

instruction.overview: Build a basic portfolio layout and add a toggle to switch between Light and Dark themes with data persistence.
steps: Design a basic layout with a header, about section, and projects.
Define CSS variables for colors (e.g., --bg-color, --text-color).
Create a state to track the current theme ('light' or 'dark').
Use the 'useEffect' hook to update the localStorage whenever the theme changes.
Ensure the app checks for the saved theme in localStorage when it first loads.
deliverables: A .zip file containing the theme-aware React project.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Verify the theme does not reset to light mode upon refreshing the page.

title: GitHub Profile Repo Fetcher
short_description: Fetch and display a list of repositories for a GitHub user using an API.
business_problem: React developers must know how to pull real-world data from external sources and handle loading states.

instruction.overview: Build a tool that asks for a username and fetches their public repositories from the GitHub API.
steps: Create an input to capture a GitHub username.
Write an asynchronous function to fetch data from '[https://api.github.com/users/USER/repos](https://api.github.com/users/USER/repos)'.
Implement a 'Loading' state to show a spinner or message while waiting.
Implement an 'Error' state for invalid usernames or network issues.
Render the list of repos as clickable links that open in a new tab.
deliverables: A .zip file with the source code and documentation.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Handle the case where a user has 0 repositories gracefully.

title: Multi-Page Site with React Router
short_description: Build a professional website with navigation between Home, About, and Contact pages.
business_problem: Single-page apps (SPAs) need client-side routing to behave like multi-page websites without the slow full-page reloads.

instruction.overview: Set up React Router and create a consistent navigation bar that changes the main content based on the URL.
steps: Install 'react-router-dom' and set up the Router provider.
Create three page components: Home, About, and Contact.
Build a Navigation component using 'Link' to avoid page refreshes.
Define routes for each component, including a '404 Not Found' page for invalid URLs.
Style the active link (e.g., bold or underlined) using 'NavLink'.
deliverables: A .zip file containing the multi-page React application.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The browser back and forward buttons must work correctly.

title: Personal Finance Dashboard
short_description: Build a complex state app to track income, expenses, and current balance.
business_problem: Financial tools require high data integrity and derived state calculations to provide accurate summaries.

instruction.overview: Develop a dashboard where users enter transactions and see calculated summaries for Income, Expenses, and Total Balance.
steps: Create a state array to store transactions with amount, description, and type (Income/Expense).
Implement a derived state (using useMemo or simple logic) to calculate the sum of all income items.
Implement a derived state to calculate the sum of all expense items.
Show the net balance (Income - Expenses) prominently at the top.
Allow users to delete a transaction and have the totals update immediately.
deliverables: A .zip file with the finance tracker project.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The balance must update instantly without manual refresh after every entry.

title: Basic Greeting API
short_description: Build a simple Node.js server that greets users based on query parameters.
business_problem: Websites need backend services to process user data and provide personalized responses.

instruction.overview: Create a Node.js server without external frameworks that accepts a 'name' parameter and returns a greeting.
steps: Import the built-in 'http' and 'url' modules.
Create a server that listens on port 3000.
Parse the incoming request URL to find the 'name' query parameter.
If a name exists, return 'Hello, [name]!'. If not, return 'Hello, Guest!'.
Set the Content-Type header to text/plain for the response.
deliverables: A single server.js file containing the code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The server must handle cases where the query string is missing.

title: Random Quote Generator Utility
short_description: Create a script that returns a random quote from a local JSON file.
business_problem: Developers need modular utilities to provide randomized content for apps and websites.

instruction.overview: Build a module that reads a list of 10 quotes from a JSON file and outputs one randomly to the terminal.
steps: Create a 'quotes.json' file with at least 10 entries.
Use the 'fs' module to read the file content asynchronously.
Parse the JSON string into a JavaScript array.
Use Math.random() to select a random index from the array.
Print the selected quote to the console.
deliverables: A script file (app.js) and the JSON data file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The script should handle file reading errors gracefully.

title: Command-Line Unit Converter
short_description: Build a CLI tool that converts units based on user arguments.
business_problem: Utility tools automate repetitive tasks for developers and system administrators.

instruction.overview: Create a command-line script that converts Kilograms to Pounds using process arguments.
steps: Access inputs using 'process.argv'.
Extract the numerical value provided as the third argument.
Validate that the input is a valid number.
Perform the conversion (1 KG = 2.204 LBS).
Print the result clearly: '[X] KG is [Y] LBS'.
deliverables: A .js file executable from the command line.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for errors when the user provides no arguments or non-numeric input.

title: File-Based Log Tracker
short_description: Create a script that appends timestamps to a local log file.
business_problem: Monitoring applications requires a reliable way to record events and timestamps for auditing.

instruction.overview: Write a script that, when run, adds a new line to 'activity.log' with the current date and time.
steps: Use the 'fs' module's append method.
Generate a readable timestamp using the Date object.
Format the string as 'Event logged at: [timestamp]\n'.
Verify that the file is created if it does not already exist.
Print a success message to the console after writing.
deliverables: A script file (logger.js) and the resulting .log file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Multiple runs should result in multiple lines in the log file.

title: Task Manager CRUD API
short_description: Build an Express API for managing a To-Do list using an in-memory array.
business_problem: CRUD operations are the foundation of modern web applications and data management systems.

instruction.overview: Develop a RESTful API using Express that allows users to create, view, update, and delete tasks.
steps: Initialize an Express app and set up body parsing middleware.
Implement GET /tasks to return the task list.
Implement POST /tasks to add a new task with a unique ID.
Implement PUT /tasks/:id to update a task's status.
Implement DELETE /tasks/:id to remove a task.
deliverables: A .zip containing package.json and the source code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for correct HTTP status codes for each operation (e.g., 201 for Created).

title: Secure User Registration Simulator
short_description: Create a registration system that hashes passwords using bcrypt.
business_problem: Storing plain-text passwords is a major security risk; developers must use industry-standard hashing.

instruction.overview: Build an Express endpoint that takes a username and password, hashes the password, and saves it to a local JSON file.
steps: Install the bcrypt library.
Create an async POST /register route.
Hash the incoming password with a salt round of 10.
Store the hashed password and username in a JSON 'database' file.
Ensure usernames are unique before saving.
deliverables: Project code with dependencies listed in package.json.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The resulting JSON file should never contain the raw password.

title: External API Weather Proxy
short_description: Build an API that fetches weather data from an external provider and returns a custom subset.
business_problem: Backend services often act as proxies to hide API keys and simplify data for frontend use.

instruction.overview: Use Axios to fetch data from OpenWeatherMap and return only the temperature and condition to the user.
steps: Sign up for a free OpenWeatherMap API key.
Create an Express GET route /weather/:city.
Perform an asynchronous request to the external API using the city param.
Extract only the 'temp' and 'main' description from the result.
Return this simplified data as a JSON response.
deliverables: A .zip containing the source code and README instructions.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The external API key should be handled securely (e.g., via environment variables).

title: Real-time Message Broadcaster
short_description: Develop a real-time notification system using Socket.io.
business_problem: Modern apps require instant communication without refreshing the page (e.g., chat, stock updates).

instruction.overview: Build a server that allows multiple clients to connect and broadcast messages to everyone in real-time.
steps: Set up an Express server and integrate Socket.io.
Create a simple HTML client to send and receive events.
Listen for a 'chat-message' event from one client on the server.
Use io.emit() to send the received message to all connected clients.
Log a message to the console when a user connects or disconnects.
deliverables: A .zip with the server code and the simple client HTML file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The message should appear on all connected browser tabs immediately without refresh.

title: Inventory System with MongoDB
short_description: Build a product inventory API using MongoDB and Mongoose.
business_problem: Scalable applications need dedicated databases to store large amounts of persistent data safely.

instruction.overview: Create an Express API that connects to MongoDB (Atlas or local) to perform operations on a 'Product' collection.
steps: Define a Mongoose schema for a product (name, price, quantity).
Establish a database connection at server startup.
Implement endpoints to Create, Read, and Update product stock levels.
Add validation to ensure 'price' is always a positive number.
Write a summary of how to set up the connection string in the README.
deliverables: A ZIP file with source code, package.json, and the Mongoose models.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Database operations should use async/await and include basic error handling.

title: URL Shortener Service
short_description: Create a service that generates short codes for long URLs and redirects them.
business_problem: Long URLs are difficult to share on social media; a shortening service improves UX and tracking.

instruction.overview: Build an app where a POST request generates a unique code for a URL, and a GET request for that code redirects to the original site.
steps: Create a POST endpoint that takes a long URL and generates a unique 6-character code.
Store the mapping in an object or local file.
Implement a GET /:code endpoint.
In the GET route, look up the original URL and use res.redirect() to send the user there.
Return a 404 error if the short code does not exist.
deliverables: The project source code and a README demonstrating sample usage.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Verify that different long URLs produce unique codes and the redirection is seamless.

title: Designing a Product Inventory Table
short_description: Create a structured database table for a retail inventory system.
business_problem: Retailers struggle to track stock when data is unorganized; a clean table structure is the first step toward automation.

instruction.overview: Design a single-table schema for a grocery store inventory, defining all necessary columns and constraints.
steps: Identify 8 essential columns for a product (e.g., ID, Name, Price).
Assign the most appropriate SQL data type to each column.
Define a Primary Key to ensure each product is unique.
Add 'NOT NULL' constraints to fields that must always have data.
Create a sample data row to demonstrate how the table will look.
deliverables: A document showing the column names, types, and sample data.
submission_requirements: Submit as a single .pdf or .docx file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the logical choice of data types for prices and descriptions.

title: Basic SQL Selection Queries for Customers
short_description: Write SQL queries to filter and sort customer records from a provided list.
business_problem: Marketing teams need specific lists of customers (e.g., by city or purchase status) to run targeted campaigns.

instruction.overview: You will write 5 SQL queries to extract meaningful data from a 'Customers' table.
steps: Write a query to select all customers living in 'New York'.
Write a query to sort customers alphabetically by their last name.
Write a query to find customers whose email addresses end in '.gov'.
Write a query to select only the 'FirstName' and 'Phone' columns.
Write a query to find all active customers registered after 2024.
deliverables: A document containing the 5 SQL code snippets.
submission_requirements: Submit a text document or PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for correct syntax and proper use of the WHERE clause.

title: Database Normalization Walkthrough
short_description: Break down a messy, redundant table into normalized forms (1NF and 2NF).
business_problem: Redundant data leads to storage waste and update anomalies where changing a value in one place misses others.

instruction.overview: Take a provided 'Flat File' of student enrollments and document the steps to normalize it.
steps: Identify columns that contain multiple values (violating 1NF) and fix them.
Identify partial dependencies where data relies on only part of a composite key.
Split the flat file into two related tables (e.g., Students and Courses).
Define the Foreign Key that links the two new tables.
Summarize why the new structure is better than the original.
deliverables: A 3-page document explaining the normalization process with 'Before' and 'After' table structures.
starter_resources: First and Second Normal Form Guide
instruction.evaluation_notes: Look for the correct separation of entities into different tables.

title: Employee Directory Schema Design
short_description: Design a schema for a company directory including departments and job roles.
business_problem: HR departments need a centralized database to manage staff information, reporting lines, and office locations.

instruction.overview: Map out the structure for an Employee database that tracks names, departments, and hire dates.
steps: Define the 'Employees' table with 10 relevant attributes.
Define a 'Departments' table to store department names and managers.
Explain how the 'Employee' table links to the 'Department' table.
Establish rules for the data (e.g., email must be unique).
Create a visual list of the tables and their connections.
deliverables: A visual diagram or a structured list of tables and columns.
submission_requirements: Submit as a PNG, JPG, or PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The link between employees and departments must be logical.

title: Entity-Relationship Diagram for Pharmacy Management
short_description: Design a relational model (ERD) to track prescriptions, patients, and doctors.
business_problem: Pharmacies need to strictly link doctors to the prescriptions they write and the patients who receive them.

instruction.overview: Create a formal ERD for a pharmacy system including Doctors, Patients, Medications, and Prescriptions.
steps: Identify the primary entities and their attributes.
Determine the cardinality of relationships (e.g., One Doctor writes Many Prescriptions).
Model the 'Prescription' entity as the bridge between Doctors, Patients, and Medications.
Mark all Primary and Foreign keys in the diagram.
Add a brief text explanation for each relationship shown.
deliverables: A visual ERD diagram and a relationship description document.
submission_requirements: Submit as a single PDF or high-resolution PNG.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluate based on the correctness of the Cardinality symbols (1:M, M:N).

title: Complex SQL Joins for Sales Reports
short_description: Write advanced SQL queries to combine data from multiple tables for business insights.
business_problem: Sales data is useless in isolation; it must be joined with product names and categories to see which items are profitable.

instruction.overview: Use a provided multi-table schema to generate 5 complex reports for a store manager.
steps: Write a query to list all order IDs alongside the Customer's Full Name using an INNER JOIN.
Write a query to calculate the total sales amount per Product Category.
Write a query to find products that have never been sold using a LEFT JOIN and a NULL check.
Write a query to count how many orders each customer has placed, sorted by order count.
Write a query to find the average price of products sold in the last 30 days.
deliverables: A document containing the 5 SQL queries and expected results explanation.
starter_resources: Grouping and Aggregating Data in SQL
instruction.evaluation_notes: The use of GROUP BY and alias names for tables is expected.

title: User Role and Access Control Schema
short_description: Design a security-focused schema to manage user logins and permissions.
business_problem: Secure apps need to differentiate between 'Admin' and 'User' to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive actions.

instruction.overview: Design a relational structure that allows a single user to have multiple roles and each role to have multiple permissions.
steps: Define 3 core tables: Users, Roles, and Permissions.
Create 'Junction Tables' (User_Roles and Role_Permissions) to handle many-to-many relationships.
Define the columns for each table, including Primary and Foreign keys.
Outline a sample data set that shows an 'Admin' role having 'Delete' permission.
Explain the logic of how a query would check if User X can perform Action Y.
deliverables: A document detailing the tables, relationships, and permission logic.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Correct implementation of junction tables is a pass/fail requirement.

title: Python CLI for SQLite Inventory Management
short_description: Write a Python script to perform CRUD operations on a local SQLite database.
business_problem: Managing data through code allows for automation and building tools for non-technical staff.

instruction.overview: Create a command-line tool that allows users to add, view, and delete items from an SQLite database.
steps: Write a Python script that connects to an 'inventory.db' file.
Implement a function to create a 'Products' table if it doesn't exist.
Add logic to take user input for product name and price, then INSERT it into the DB.
Implement a view function that uses a SELECT query and prints items to the terminal.
Include error handling to prevent the script from crashing during invalid inputs.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the .py script and the generated .db file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Building a simple CLI in Python
instruction.evaluation_notes: The code must be clean, use functions, and follow the CODE project guidelines.

title: Automated SQL Data Migration Script
short_description: Write a script to transform and move data from a JSON file into a relational database.
business_problem: Data often arrives in messy formats (like JSON) and needs to be structured and migrated to a production database.

instruction.overview: Develop a script that reads a 'users.json' file and inserts the records into a structured SQL table.
steps: Create a 'users.json' with sample data for 10 users.
Write Python code to open and parse the JSON file.
Establish a database connection and ensure the target table is ready.
Map the JSON fields to the corresponding SQL columns.
Use 'parameterized queries' to insert the data safely (avoiding SQL injection).
deliverables: A ZIP file with the migration script, JSON source, and database file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Security is key; no direct string concatenation for SQL queries should be used.

title: Database Indexing and Query Performance Audit
short_description: Identify slow queries and create an indexing strategy to improve database speed.
business_problem: As databases grow, simple queries can become slow; indexing is the primary way to maintain high performance.

instruction.overview: Perform a mock performance audit on a slow database and recommend an indexing plan.
steps: Analyze a scenario where a search for 'Order Date' in a million-row table is taking 5 seconds.
Explain the 'EXPLAIN' command and how it shows the query execution plan.
Identify columns that are frequently used in WHERE and JOIN clauses.
Propose 3 specific indexes (including one 'Composite Index') to speed up searches.
Describe the trade-off of indexing (e.g., impact on INSERT/UPDATE speed).
deliverables: A 5-page performance audit report with technical recommendations.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluate based on the technical justification of the chosen index columns.

title: Software Requirements Specification (SRS) for a Task App
short_description: Draft a formal SRS document defining the features and constraints for a mobile to-do list.
business_problem: Developers often build features that users don't need because requirements were never clearly documented or agreed upon.

instruction.overview: Create a 3-page SRS document for a simple 'Daily Planner' application following standard IEEE-style sections.
steps: Define the project scope and primary objective.
List 5 essential functional requirements (what the system must do).
List 3 non-functional requirements (performance, security, usability).
Draft 2 user stories in the format: 'As a [user], I want to [action] so that [benefit]'.
Identify at least 2 technical constraints (e.g., must run on Android 10+).
deliverables: A structured SRS document.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the clarity and testability of the requirements.

title: Writing Basic Unit Tests in Python
short_description: Create a suite of automated tests to verify the logic of a simple calculator module.
business_problem: Manual testing is slow and prone to error; automated unit tests ensure that changes to code don't break existing features.

instruction.overview: You will write unit tests for a provided (or self-written) Python script containing addition, subtraction, and division functions.
steps: Identify the 'unhappy paths' (e.g., division by zero).
Use Python's built-in 'unittest' library to create a test class.
Write 3 tests for positive scenarios (valid math).
Write 2 tests for edge cases or error scenarios.
Verify all tests pass in your local environment.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the calculator code and the test script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Tests should correctly identify failures when math logic is intentionally broken.

title: Bug Lifecycle and Reporting Documentation
short_description: Analyze a software defect and document its full lifecycle in a formal bug report.
business_problem: Vague bug reports waste developer time; structured reports allow teams to reproduce and fix issues faster.

instruction.overview: Select a minor bug in a website or app and write a professional report following the standard defect lifecycle.
steps: Find a UI or logic bug (e.g., a button that doesn't click, or a typo).
Define the 'Severity' (impact on system) and 'Priority' (urgency to fix).
List clear, numbered steps to reproduce the bug.
Contrast the 'Actual Result' with the 'Expected Result'.
Suggest a simple fix or technical cause.
deliverables: A structured Bug Report document.
starter_resources: How to write a great bug report
instruction.evaluation_notes: The 'Steps to Reproduce' must be clear enough for a third party to follow exactly.

title: Application Logic Flowchart Design
short_description: Visualize the logical flow of a user authentication system using standard symbols.
business_problem: Developers need to understand the logic of a system before they can code it correctly; diagrams prevent logic errors.

instruction.overview: Create a logic flowchart for a login process, including 'Forgot Password' and 'Incorrect Credentials' paths.
steps: Use standard flowchart symbols (Ovals for Start/End, Diamonds for Decisions).
Map the 'Success' path where a user enters the correct details.
Map the 'Failure' path for an incorrect password (limit 3 attempts).
Include the logic for checking if the account is locked.
Add a brief text summary explaining the flow.
deliverables: A visual flowchart image or PDF.
submission_requirements: Submit as a single PNG or PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The decision diamonds must have clear 'Yes' and 'No' branch labels.

title: Code Review and Refactoring for Clean Code
short_description: Analyze a piece of 'spaghetti code' and refactor it for better readability and maintainability.
business_problem: Legacy code is often messy and hard to update; refactoring reduces technical debt and makes future development cheaper.

instruction.overview: You will take a provided long, unorganized function and break it into smaller, well-named sub-functions.
steps: Identify 3 'code smells' in the original snippet (e.g., hardcoded values, nested if-statements).
Apply the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle to redundant logic.
Rename variables from generic names (like 'x' or 'data') to descriptive ones.
Ensure the final output has the same functionality as the original.
Write a summary of the improvements made.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the 'Before' code, the 'After' refactored code, and a README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Clean Code by Robert C. Martin (Summary)
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluate based on the reduction of 'cyclomatic complexity' and improved readability.

title: High-Level System Architecture Diagram
short_description: Design a 3-tier architecture diagram for a web-based e-commerce platform.
business_problem: Architectural diagrams help teams communicate how different parts of a system interact, ensuring the infrastructure supports the software.

instruction.overview: Create a professional diagram showing the components and data flow for a web shop.
steps: Define the layers: Frontend, Backend API, and Database.
Show how the user interacts with the Frontend via a browser.
Show the connection between the Backend and an external Payment Gateway API.
Identify where specific data is stored (e.g., User Data in SQL, Product Images in Object Storage).
Add short annotations for each connection (e.g., 'JSON over HTTPS').
deliverables: A system architecture diagram PDF.
submission_requirements: Submit as a single PDF file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Diagram should clearly separate concerns and show directional flow of data.

title: RESTful API Documentation (OpenAPI)
short_description: Write a formal technical specification for a Product Catalog API.
business_problem: External developers cannot use an API without clear documentation on endpoints, parameters, and responses.

instruction.overview: Create a detailed technical manual for an API that manages products (List, View, Create).
steps: Define 3 endpoints: GET /products, GET /products/{id}, and POST /products.
For each, specify the required header (e.g., Content-Type).
Document the expected JSON request body for the POST request.
List at least 3 possible HTTP response codes (200, 201, 404) and their meanings.
Provide a 'curl' or 'fetch' example for one of the endpoints.
deliverables: A 3-4 page API Documentation PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Format should look professional and mimic real developer documentation.

title: Implementation of Creational Design Patterns
short_description: Code a small project that uses the Singleton and Factory design patterns.
business_problem: Ad-hoc object creation makes code rigid; design patterns provide proven solutions to common structural problems.

instruction.overview: Demonstrate the use of patterns by building a 'Shape' factory and a single 'Logger' instance.
steps: Implement a Logger class using the Singleton pattern to ensure only one log file exists.
Create an interface or base class called 'Shape'.
Implement concrete classes (Circle, Square) that inherit from 'Shape'.
Create a 'ShapeFactory' class that returns an instance of a shape based on a string input.
Write a main test script that uses both patterns together.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing all class files and a README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The Singleton must correctly prevent multiple instantiations (e.g., private constructor).

title: Continuous Integration (CI) Pipeline Automation
short_description: Create a configuration file to automate code testing on every push.
business_problem: Manually running tests for every change is unsustainable as teams grow; CI pipelines catch errors automatically before deployment.

instruction.overview: Write a workflow YAML file (e.g., GitHub Actions) that installs dependencies and runs unit tests for a Python project.
steps: Define the trigger event (e.g., 'on: push').
Specify the environment/runner (e.g., 'ubuntu-latest').
Add a step to check out the code from the repository.
Add a step to install requirements from a requirements.txt file.
Add the final step to run the testing command (e.g., 'pytest' or 'python -m unittest').
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the .yaml config file and a README explanation.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The syntax of the YAML file must be valid and logical.

title: Software Security and Vulnerability Audit
short_description: Conduct a mock security review of a web application and propose mitigation strategies.
business_problem: Security breaches are catastrophic for business; engineers must proactively find and fix vulnerabilities like SQL injection or XSS.

instruction.overview: You will analyze a provided code snippet (or descriptive scenario) and identify 5 major security risks.
steps: Identify 5 vulnerabilities based on the OWASP Top 10 (e.g., Broken Access Control).
Explain how an attacker could exploit each vulnerability.
Describe the business impact of each potential exploit (e.g., data theft).
Provide specific code-level solutions to 'mitigate' each risk.
List 3 tools used by security professionals to scan for these issues.
deliverables: A 6-page professional security audit report.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation focuses on the depth of the technical solutions provided.

title: Hosting a Static Website on Cloud Storage
short_description: Configure a cloud storage bucket to host and serve a basic static website.
business_problem: Small businesses need a cost-effective way to host simple landing pages without managing full virtual servers.

instruction.overview: You will set up a cloud storage bucket (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob) to serve a static index.html file to the public.
steps: Create a storage bucket with a unique name.
Upload a simple index.html file with a 'Welcome' message.
Modify bucket permissions to allow public read access.
Enable the 'Static Website Hosting' feature in the bucket settings.
Verify the site is live by visiting the provided public endpoint URL.
deliverables: A screenshot showing the public URL and the rendered webpage.
submission_requirements: Submit one PDF or image file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the correct configuration of public access permissions.

title: Comparison of Cloud Service Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
short_description: Research and document the differences between the three main cloud service models.
business_problem: Companies often choose the wrong service model, leading to unnecessary management overhead or a lack of control.

instruction.overview: Create a report that defines IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS, providing one real-world example for each.
steps: Define each service model in plain language.
List 3 things the customer manages vs. 3 things the provider manages for each model.
Identify one major provider for each model (e.g., AWS, Salesforce, Heroku).
Describe a scenario where a startup should prefer PaaS over IaaS.
deliverables: A 2-page research report.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Ensure the distinction between management responsibilities is accurate.

title: IAM Policy for Least Privilege
short_description: Draft a cloud security policy that grants minimal access to a junior developer.
business_problem: Over-privileged users are a major security risk; cloud engineers must restrict access to only what is necessary.

instruction.overview: Write a JSON-style policy that allows a user to 'Read' and 'List' objects in a specific bucket but 'Deny' deleting them.
steps: Identify the 'Actions' required for listing and reading cloud objects.
Draft the 'Statement' block including Effect, Action, and Resource.
Use a wildcard (*) only where absolutely necessary.
Write a brief explanation of why 'Least Privilege' is important in cloud security.
deliverables: A JSON policy block and a written security explanation.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The JSON must be valid and the 'Action' list must not include 'Delete'.

title: Cloud Cost Estimation for a Small Application
short_description: Use a cloud pricing calculator to estimate monthly costs for a basic web setup.
business_problem: Unexpected cloud bills can bankrupt a startup; accurate forecasting is a required business skill.

instruction.overview: Generate a cost estimate for 1 Virtual Machine, 100GB of Storage, and a Load Balancer for one month.
steps: Use an official Cloud Calculator (AWS Pricing Calculator or similar).
Add an 'On-Demand' micro-instance for the server.
Add standard block storage and 50GB of data transfer.
Export the summary and transfer the data into a spreadsheet for formatting.
Highlight the cost impact of switching to a 'Reserved Instance' for 1 year.
deliverables: A formatted spreadsheet showing line-item costs and totals.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Check for accurate math and inclusion of data transfer costs.

title: Python Script for Automatic S3 Backups
short_description: Write a script that uploads all files from a local directory to a cloud bucket.
business_problem: Manual backups are unreliable; automation ensures that local data is always safely replicated to the cloud.

instruction.overview: Create a Python utility using the Boto3 library (or equivalent) to sync a local 'backup' folder to a cloud bucket.
steps: Install the cloud SDK library (e.g., pip install boto3).
Write a loop to iterate through every file in a local directory.
Implement a function that uploads each file using its local name as the key.
Add basic error handling for failed uploads.
Print a summary of files successfully uploaded.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the backup script and a sample directory structure.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The script should not contain hardcoded access keys (placeholders are okay).

title: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Network Diagram
short_description: Design a secure network architecture with public and private subnets.
business_problem: Placing databases in public subnets is a security failure; developers must understand how to isolate resources.

instruction.overview: Design a 2-tier network diagram for a web app where the Web Server is public and the Database is private.
