instruction.overview: Build a modular inventory script that handles picking up, dropping, and 'using' items.
steps: Create an 'Item' base class with attributes like weight and value.
Implement specific types (Weapon, Consumable) using inheritance.
Write logic for an 'Inventory' class with a maximum weight capacity.
Add functions to 'Pick Up' (add to list) and 'Drop' (remove from list).
Ensure stats (like Health) update when a 'Consumable' is used.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the class scripts and a CLI test script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The weight-limit logic must be accurate.

title: A* Pathfinding Visualizer
short_description: Implement and visualize the A* algorithm finding the shortest path around obstacles.
business_problem: AI enemies that get stuck on walls ruin immersion; pathfinding is the 'nervous system' of game AI.

instruction.overview: Create a grid-based tool where a 'Start' point finds the 'End' point while avoiding 'Wall' nodes.
steps: Implement the A* algorithm logic using f, g, and h scores.
Visualize the 'Open' and 'Closed' nodes in real-time.
Allow the user to 'Draw' walls on the grid with their mouse.
Calculate the shortest path and highlight it in a distinct color.
Measure and display the time taken for the calculation.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the interactive code project.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The algorithm must never fail to find a path if one exists.

title: Tic-Tac-Toe with Minimax AI
short_description: Build an unbeatable Tic-Tac-Toe game using the Minimax recursive algorithm.
business_problem: Designing AI that can 'think' ahead is a foundational skill for turn-based strategy games.

instruction.overview: Create a 3x3 board where a user plays against an AI that always chooses the optimal move.
steps: Represent the board as a 1D or 2D array.
Write a function to check for win/draw conditions.
Implement the Minimax function to score potential board states.
Add a visual interface (CLI or Web) to show the moves.
Test the AI to ensure it never loses (it should only win or tie).
deliverables: A ZIP file with the AI script and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The AI should be able to block the user from winning in all scenarios.

title: Top-Down Enemy AI State Machine
short_description: Develop a logic system for an enemy that switches between Idle, Patrol, and Chase states.
business_problem: Hard-coding complex AI behavior is impossible; State Machines provide a clean, scalable way to manage NPC logic.

instruction.overview: Create a script for a 2D/3D enemy that changes behavior based on the player's proximity.
steps: Define an Enum for the three states (Idle, Patrol, Chase).
Implement a 'Patrol' function that moves the enemy between two points.
Implement a detection check (Distance < Threshold) to trigger the 'Chase' state.
Add a 'Return to Patrol' logic if the player escapes the radius.
Use console logs to show state transitions in real-time.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the state machine script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Transitions between states must be smooth and logical.

title: Procedural Dungeon Generation Algorithm
short_description: Write a script that generates a random, connected layout of rooms and corridors.
business_problem: Manually designing hundreds of levels is too expensive; procedural generation creates infinite replayability.

instruction.overview: Develop an algorithm (like Binary Space Partitioning) to create a map of connected rectangular rooms.
steps: Initialize a large grid filled with 'Wall' tiles.
Recursively split the grid into smaller sub-sections (BSP).
Place a room of random size within each sub-section.
Write a function to connect rooms with L-shaped corridors.
Output the final map to a text file or console using characters (e.g., # and .).
deliverables: A ZIP file with the generation script and sample outputs.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: All rooms must be reachable from one another (no isolated areas).

title: Physics-Based Platformer Controller
short_description: Build a responsive character controller that handles jumping, gravity, and momentum.
business_problem: The 'feel' of movement is the most critical part of an action game; a clunky controller ruins the user experience.

instruction.overview: Develop a script that moves a character based on player input, including 'coyote time' or smooth acceleration.
steps: Implement horizontal movement with acceleration and friction.
Create a gravity system that pulls the character down.
Implement a 'Jump' function that works only when grounded.
Add a 'Ground Check' using raycasts or simple collision detection.
Ensure movement speed is independent of the frame rate.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the controller script.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
starter_resources: Making a jump feel good guide
instruction.evaluation_notes: Movement should feel 'snappy' rather than 'floaty'.

title: Post-Processing Shader Effect Design
short_description: Write a shader to create a 'Vignette' or 'Grayscale' effect on the screen.
business_problem: Visual polish is achieved through shaders; they allow for high-performance visual effects without manual image editing.

instruction.overview: Develop a fragment shader that modifies the final rendered frame to create a specific visual style.
steps: Define a 'Grayscale' calculation using the dot product of the RGB color and luma weights.
Implement a 'Vignette' by calculating the distance from the center of the screen.
Create a 'Mix' function to allow a user to toggle the intensity of the effect.
Optimize the shader to minimize texture lookups.
Provide the code for the .shader or .frag file.
deliverables: The shader source code and a README with instructions.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The shader must be efficient and not cause significant frame-rate drops.

title: Multiplayer Game Lobby Prototype
short_description: Build a network-syncing prototype where players can join a room and see each other.
business_problem: Modern games rely on social play; mastering networking is essential for competitive and cooperative gaming.

instruction.overview: Create a basic server-client system using WebSockets (like Socket.io) to track player positions.
steps: Set up a Node.js server that listens for incoming connections.
Broadcast the arrival of a new player to all other connected clients.
Implement a 'Heartbeat' system to detect disconnected players.
Sync player position $(x, y)$ every 100ms.
Add basic 'Client-Side Prediction' to mask network lag.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the server and client code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the efficiency of the data packets sent over the wire.

title: Binary Game Save and Load Manager
short_description: Implement a system that saves character state into a compact binary format.
business_problem: Plain-text save files (like JSON) are easy for players to hack; binary formats are more secure and faster to load.

instruction.overview: Develop a script that serializes a 'PlayerStats' object into a non-human-readable file and loads it back.
steps: Define a 'Player' structure with Level, HP, and Inventory array.
Write a 'SaveGame' function that writes this data to a .dat file.
Write a 'LoadGame' function that parses the binary data back into the structure.
Add a 'Checksum' or simple validation to prevent loading corrupted files.
Compare the file size of the binary version vs. a JSON version of the same data.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the save/load script and a sample data file.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The binary file must accurately restore the player state without data loss.

title: Simple Solidity Greeting Contract
short_description: Write a smart contract that stores and updates a greeting message on the blockchain.
business_problem: Decentralized applications need a way to store and modify state variables securely without a central server.

instruction.overview: Develop a Solidity contract that allows a user to save a string and retrieve it later.
steps: Define a version pragma at the top of your file.
Create a state variable to store the message.
Implement a constructor to set an initial greeting.
Write a function to update the message.
Write a 'view' function to return the current message.
deliverables: A .sol file containing the contract code.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The contract must compile without errors in a standard environment.

title: ERC-20 Token Specification Report
short_description: Define the parameters and supply mechanics for a custom utility token.
business_problem: Startups need to plan their token's economic structure before deployment to ensure long-term sustainability.

instruction.overview: Draft a formal technical specification for a new ERC-20 token.
steps: Define the Token Name, Symbol (Ticker), and Decimals.
State the Total and Max Supply of the token.
Outline a distribution plan (e.g., 20% for the team, 50% for public).
Describe at least 3 specific use cases for the token within an ecosystem.
Explain the 'Burn' or 'Inflation' mechanics if applicable.
deliverables: A 3-page Token Specification PDF.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the logical consistency of the distribution percentages.

title: Blockchain Fundamental Concepts Quiz
short_description: Develop a set of 10 questions explaining nodes, consensus, and immutability.
business_problem: Internal training for non-technical staff is required to build a shared understanding of blockchain value propositions.

instruction.overview: Create a multiple-choice quiz that tests core blockchain knowledge.
steps: Draft 10 questions covering distributed ledgers and peer-to-peer networks.
Include a mix of 'What is' and 'How does X work' questions.
Provide 4 options for each question.
Create an answer key with brief explanations for each correct answer.
Explain the difference between a public and private blockchain in one question.
deliverables: A document containing the quiz and answer key.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Questions should be technically accurate and unambiguous.

title: Multi-Signature Wallet Contract Logic
short_description: Implement a contract that requires approval from multiple owners to release funds.
business_problem: Single-owner wallets are a single point of failure; multi-sig wallets protect funds from theft or accidental loss.

instruction.overview: Build a Solidity contract that allows $m$ of $n$ owners to authorize a transaction.
steps: Define an array of owner addresses and a required threshold number.
Implement a 'submitTransaction' function to propose a payment.
Implement a 'confirmTransaction' function for other owners to sign off.
Implement an 'executeTransaction' function that only works if the threshold is met.
Ensure only owners can interact with the critical functions.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the smart contract and a README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Security is paramount; ensure no unauthorized person can confirm transactions.

title: On-Chain Escrow System
short_description: Develop a smart contract to hold funds until both a buyer and seller confirm a deal.
business_problem: Freelance and trade transactions need a trustless third party to prevent payment fraud.

instruction.overview: Build a contract that manages the states: AWAITING_PAYMENT, AWAITING_DELIVERY, and COMPLETE.
steps: Use an 'Enum' to track the contract state.
Implement a 'deposit' function where the buyer sends funds.
Implement a 'confirmDelivery' function where the buyer releases funds to the seller.
Add a 'refund' function only accessible if the seller agrees or an arbiter intervenes.
Calculate and deduct a small 'platform fee' upon completion.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the contract and test cases.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The funds should be locked in the contract until a specific state transition occurs.

title: NFT Marketplace Metadata Schema
short_description: Design a JSON metadata structure and IPFS storage strategy for an NFT collection.
business_problem: NFTs are only as good as their data; inconsistent metadata makes items invisible or broken on major marketplaces.

instruction.overview: Design an ERC-721 compatible metadata schema for a digital art collection.
steps: Create a sample JSON object including Name, Description, and Image link.
Add a list of 'Attributes' or 'Traits' (e.g., Color, Rarity).
Explain how the image and JSON will be stored on IPFS to ensure decentralization.
Describe how the 'tokenURI' function in a smart contract will link to this data.
Draft a strategy for updating metadata (or locking it permanently).
deliverables: A technical schema document and sample JSON file.
starter_resources: IPFS Best Practices for NFT Developers
instruction.evaluation_notes: The schema must strictly follow the standards used by modern NFT platforms.

title: AMM Liquidity Pool Math Audit
short_description: Analyze and calculate the impact of trades on a Constant Product liquidity pool.
business_problem: DeFi users must understand slippage and price impact to avoid losing value during large swaps.

instruction.overview: Perform a mathematical audit on a liquidity pool swap scenario using the formula $x dot y = k$.
steps: Define an initial pool with 1,000 Token A and 1,000 Token B.
Calculate the new price of Token A after a user buys 100 Token A from the pool.
Calculate the 'Slippage' percentage for this specific trade.
Explain how adding more liquidity (doubling the pool) affects the slippage of the same 100-token trade.
Summarize the relationship between pool depth and price stability.
deliverables: A 5-page mathematical audit report.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Accuracy in the algebraic calculations is critical for a passing score.

title: Smart Contract Security Audit (Reentrancy)
short_description: Identify a reentrancy vulnerability in a provided contract and implement a fix.
business_problem: Security bugs in smart contracts have led to losses of hundreds of millions of dollars; auditing is a required skill for any developer.

instruction.overview: Analyze a vulnerable 'Bank' contract and refactor it to prevent recursive withdrawal attacks.
steps: Locate the line of code that allows a caller to re-enter the contract before state update.
Draft a mock 'Attacker' contract that exploits the flaw.
Apply the 'Checks-Effects-Interactions' pattern to the vulnerable function.
Implement a 'ReentrancyGuard' modifier as a second layer of defense.
Document the fix and explain why the original code failed.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the original, attacker, and fixed contracts.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The fix must be technically perfect and address the root cause.

title: Cross-Chain Bridge Strategy Design
short_description: Design the technical architecture for moving tokens between two different blockchains.
business_problem: Liquidity is fragmented across chains; bridges are necessary for a unified decentralized economy.

instruction.overview: Create a high-level system design for a 'Lock-and-Mint' bridge.
steps: Diagram the flow from Chain A (Source) to Chain B (Destination).
Describe the role of 'Relayers' or 'Oracles' in verifying the source transaction.
Identify the primary security risk (e.g., Centralized Relayers) and suggest a mitigation.
Explain how the system handles 'Reorgs' or finality issues on the source chain.
Draft the logic for a 'Redeem' request to move tokens back to the original chain.
deliverables: A system architecture diagram and a 6-page design document PDF.
starter_resources: Vitalik Buterin's views on Cross-Chain security
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation focuses on the robustness of the verification logic.

title: DAO Governance Smart Contract
short_description: Develop a system for proposal creation and voting weighted by token ownership.
business_problem: Decentralized organizations need automated rules for decision-making without a central CEO.

instruction.overview: Build a contract where users can propose actions and others vote using their token balance.
steps: Link the contract to an existing ERC-20 token.
Create a 'Proposal' struct with a description and target action.
Implement a 'vote' function that uses the sender's current balance as their weight.
Define a 'Quorum' (minimum total votes) and 'Majority' requirement.
Write logic to 'execute' the proposal only if it passes all checks after the voting period.
deliverables: A ZIP file containing the governance contracts and README.
submission_requirements: Code projects must be submitted as one .zip upload only.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Verify that votes are tallied correctly based on the weight of tokens.

title: Low-Fidelity Wireframes for a Pet Adoption App
short_description: Sketch the primary user flow for finding and applying to adopt a pet.
business_problem: Jumping into high-fidelity design too early leads to wasted effort on layouts that don't serve the user flow.

instruction.overview: Create a set of 5 wireframes representing the main screens of a pet adoption app.
steps: Identify 5 key screens (e.g., Home, Search Results, Pet Details, Application Form).
Sketch the layout for each screen, focusing on content placement over colors.
Define the primary navigation method (e.g., Tab bar or Hamburger menu).
Show how a user moves from 'Home' to 'Submitting an Application'.
Annotate the wireframes to explain the purpose of each section.
deliverables: A PDF or image set of the 5 wireframes.
submission_requirements: Submit a single .pdf or image file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the logical arrangement of buttons and information.

title: Accessible Color Palette Design
short_description: Create a brand color palette that meets WCAG 2.1 contrast standards.
business_problem: Inaccessible designs exclude users with visual impairments and can lead to legal compliance issues.

instruction.overview: Develop a professional color scheme for a medical portal and verify its accessibility.
steps: Select a Primary, Secondary, and Accent color.
Determine the Background and Text colors for the UI.
Use a contrast checker to ensure the text-on-background ratio is at least 4.5:1.
Document the Hex codes for each color.
Explain why these specific colors are appropriate for a 'Medical Portal' (psychology of color).
deliverables: A Color Palette document including contrast test results.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Contrast ratio verification is the most important part of this task.

title: Responsive Landing Page Layout
short_description: Design a hero section that adapts from desktop to mobile screens.
business_problem: Websites must be usable on all devices; a layout that breaks on mobile leads to lost customers.

instruction.overview: Create a visual design for a landing page hero section in both Desktop and Mobile views.
steps: Design the desktop view (1440px wide) with a headline, CTA, and image.
Design the mobile view (375px wide) showing how the elements reorder.
Ensure the text remains readable on the smaller screen.
Show the 'hamburger' menu state for the mobile view.
Indicate which elements scale vs. which elements stack vertically.
deliverables: A design mockup showing both views side-by-side.
submission_requirements: Submit a single PDF or PNG file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the 'Visual Hierarchy' and readability across both sizes.

title: User Persona & Journey for a FinTech App
short_description: Define a target user and map their emotional journey through a budget tracking app.
business_problem: Developing features without understanding the user's emotional state leads to poor engagement and high churn.

instruction.overview: Create a 4-page UX research document for a new 'Savings' app.
steps: Define a detailed 'User Persona' (Age, Goals, Frustrations).
Identify the primary 'Trigger' that makes them open the app.
Map the journey from 'Initial Sign-up' to 'Setting a Savings Goal'.
Document the 'Emotional State' at each touchpoint (e.g., Anxious during sign-up, Satisfied when goal is set).
List 3 'Design Opportunities' discovered through the journey map.
deliverables: A comprehensive UX Discovery report.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The journey map must identify realistic pain points for a finance user.

title: Interactive High-Fi Prototype
short_description: Build a clickable prototype showing transitions between three main screens.
business_problem: Static designs can't communicate the 'feel' of an app; prototypes allow stakeholders to test functionality before coding.

instruction.overview: Create an interactive prototype for a 'Task Manager' app.
steps: Design 3 screens: Dashboard, Add Task Modal, and Task Details.
Connect the buttons to trigger transitions between the screens.
Use 'Smart Animate' or similar to show smooth modal pop-ups.
Include a 'Back' button on all sub-screens.
Provide a shareable link or record a video of the flow.
deliverables: A shareable link to the prototype or a video recording (.mp4).
submission_requirements: Submit a text file with the link or a .zip with the video.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The prototype must be fully functional and 'loop' correctly (no dead ends).

title: Micro-interaction for Mobile Buttons
short_description: Design the visual feedback states for a single 'Add to Cart' button.
business_problem: Users need immediate confirmation of their actions; micro-interactions provide the 'satisfaction' and feedback needed for good UX.

instruction.overview: Design 5 distinct states for a primary action button.
steps: Default State: The standard button appearance.
Hover/Active State: How it looks when a finger/mouse is over it.
Pressed State: The visual 'click' feedback.
Loading State: A spinner or progress bar inside the button.
Success State: A checkmark or color change after the action completes.
deliverables: A single image or PDF showing all 5 button states.
submission_requirements: Submit as a PNG or PDF file.
instruction.evaluation_notes: Contrast and clarity of the 'Success' state are key.

title: Design System Component Library
short_description: Build a library of reusable UI components (Inputs, Buttons, Cards) for a large app.
business_problem: Scaling an app without a design system leads to 'design debt', where every page looks and behaves differently.

instruction.overview: Create an 'Atoms' and 'Molecules' library in Figma using the Atomic Design methodology.
steps: Define 'Atoms': Typography, Colors, Icons, and basic Button shapes.
Define 'Molecules': Search bars, Input fields with labels, and Navigation links.
Use 'Variants' to manage different sizes and states of each component.
Implement 'Auto-Layout' so components resize based on content.
Write a 1-page usage guide for developers.
deliverables: A ZIP file with the design export and documentation.
starter_resources: Building a design system in Figma
instruction.evaluation_notes: Evaluation is based on the 'reusability' and organization of the file.

title: UX Audit for a Complex Dashboard
short_description: Identify usability issues in an existing data dashboard and propose improvements.
business_problem: Dashboards with too much info lead to 'cognitive overload', making it hard for users to find the data they need.

instruction.overview: Analyze a provided (or chosen) complex dashboard and write a detailed audit report.
steps: Evaluate the dashboard using Nielsen's 10 Heuristics.
Identify 3 areas where 'Information Density' is too high.
Propose 5 specific UI changes to improve the 'Signal-to-Noise' ratio.
Explain how the use of 'Progressive Disclosure' could help.
Sketch a 'Before' and 'After' wireframe for the main dashboard view.
deliverables: A 6-page professional UX Audit report (PDF).
instruction.evaluation_notes: The report must provide actionable technical recommendations, not just vague 'make it prettier' advice.

title: Information Architecture (IA) for a University Portal
short_description: Map out the structure and navigation of a large, content-heavy website.
business_problem: Poor IA makes it impossible for users to find the specific info they need (e.g., student records vs. course catalogs).

instruction.overview: Create a comprehensive Sitemap and Navigation Map for a university website.
steps: Identify 3 distinct user groups (Student, Professor, Prospective Parent).
Map out the Top-Level and Second-Level navigation pages.
Design the 'Taxonomy' for a course catalog (how categories and tags are organized).
Explain the 'Labeling System' used (why specific names were chosen for menu items).
Create a visual diagram showing the 'Search' vs. 'Browse' paths.
deliverables: A visual Sitemap and a 5-page IA strategy document.
instruction.evaluation_notes: The map should be logical and account for the different needs of each user group.

title: Heuristic Evaluation of a SaaS Product
short_description: Perform a rigorous expert review of a software-as-a-service application.
business_problem: SaaS tools are used for work; even minor friction adds up to hours of lost productivity for the end-user.
expected_keywords: match between system and real world

instruction.overview: Choose a project management tool (e.g., Trello or Jira) and audit its onboarding flow.
steps: Document the 10-step onboarding process with screenshots.
Score each step based on relevant heuristics.
Identify the 'Moment of Value' where the user understands the tool.
Propose 3 ways to shorten the time-to-value.
Draft a 200-word summary of the audit findings for a product manager.
deliverables: A 10-page expert review case study (PDF).
instruction.evaluation_notes: Focus on the 'Severity' rating given to each identified issue.
